item.text:
**4B.10 Research Note: Bola Ahmed Tinubu (2024)**

Bottom line: **weaker overall**. I did not find evidence of a term-limit violation or a broken constitutional transfer of power, but 2024 still looks net negative for democratic resilience because the government combined some pro-institution rhetoric with sustained harassment of protesters, journalists, and online critics. The inherited baseline was already only partly free, so this is a decline at the margins rather than regime collapse.

**Accepted Claims**

- [President Tinubu Receives Patriot Group, Says Strengthening Nigeria’s Economy a Topmost Priority but Request for New Constitution Will Be Reviewed](https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-receives-patriot-group-says-strengthening-nigerias-economy-a-topmost-priority-but-request-for-new-constitution-will-be-reviewed/) — State House, August 9, 2024. Tinubu said a request for a constituent assembly and new constitution would be reviewed, and framed constitutional change as the way to manage diversity and avoid conflict. This is the clearest positive sign that he preferred constitutional channels over extra-constitutional rule change. QIDs: `4B.10`, `4B.8`.

- [Nigeria: Freedom on the Net 2024 Country Report](https://freedomhouse.org/country/nigeria/freedom-net/2024) — Freedom House, 2024. Freedom House said there were no internet connectivity shutdowns during the coverage period. That is a real positive for resilience, though it is limited by simultaneous digital-law pressure and content control. QIDs: `4B.10`, `4B.9`.

- [Tinubu’s call for collaboration on governance splits opposition parties](https://guardian.ng/politics/tinubus-call-for-collaboration-on-governance-splits-opposition-parties/) — The Guardian Nigeria, January 7, 2024. Tinubu’s “election is over, it’s time for all of us to work together” message signaled post-election coalition-building, even as opposition figures warned it could drift toward one-party dominance. QIDs: `4B.10`, `4B.8`, `4B.5`.

- [President Tinubu Receives U.S. Ambassador, Underscores Importance of Sustaining Democracy, Its Norms and Institutions](https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-receives-u-s-ambassador-underscores-importance-of-sustaining-democracy-its-norms-and-institutions/) — State House, July 25, 2024. Tinubu said protests are part of democracy and only drew a line at destruction of lives and property. This is pro-democratic rhetoric, but it is general and not proof of durable strengthening. QIDs: `4B.10`, `4B.1`, `4B.3`, `4B.7`.

- [President Tinubu’s Broadcast on the Nationwide Protest](https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubus-broadcast-on-the-nationwide-protest/) — State House, August 4, 2024. Tinubu acknowledged protesters’ legitimate hopes, asked them to suspend demonstrations for dialogue, and told law enforcement to protect lives and property responsibly. This is the strongest restraint signal in 2024, but it was reactive and paired with later coercive enforcement. QIDs: `4B.10`, `4B.1`, `4B.3`, `4B.7`.

- [Nigeria’s Tinubu names seven ministers, sacks five in cabinet reshuffle](https://theprint.in/world/nigerias-tinubu-names-seven-ministers-sacks-five-in-cabinet-reshuffle/2325625/) — Reuters via ThePrint, October 23, 2024. Reuters described an ordinary cabinet reshuffle, which is weak positive evidence against arbitrary purge or loyalty-testing behavior. It does not, by itself, prove stronger democratic resilience. QIDs: `4B.10`, `4B.5`, `4B.8`.

- [Nigeria: Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report](https://freedomhouse.org/country/nigeria/freedom-world/2024) — Freedom House, 2024. Freedom House said Nigeria’s media environment is impeded by criminal defamation laws and frequent harassment and arrest of journalists covering politically sensitive topics. This is evidence that democratic resilience was not strengthened in the public-sphere dimension. QIDs: `4B.10`, `4B.6`, `4B.7`.

- [Nigeria: Freedom on the Net 2024 Country Report](https://freedomhouse.org/country/nigeria/freedom-net/2024) — Freedom House, 2024. Freedom House said February 2024 cybercrime amendments centralized traffic through SOC/CERT architecture, and that police were told to monitor and prosecute “false information.” It also noted blocking of cryptocurrency sites and some inaccessible political websites. That is strong negative evidence on digital freedom and institutional restraint. QIDs: `4B.10`, `4B.6`, `4B.9`, `4B.5`.

- [Nigeria has detained a journalist who reported on corruption in a widening crackdown](https://www.gpb.org/news/2024/05/09/nigeria-has-detained-journalist-who-reported-on-corruption-in-widening-crackdown) — Reuters via GPB, May 9, 2024. Reuters reported journalist Daniel Ojukwu was detained under the Cybercrime Act after corruption reporting, which shows administrative harassment of independent journalism. QIDs: `4B.10`, `4B.6`, `4B.9`, `4B.5`.

- [Nigeria police charge 4 journalists with cybercrimes for corruption reporting](https://cpj.org/2024/10/nigeria-police-charge-4-journalists-with-cybercrimes-for-corruption-reporting/) — Committee to Protect Journalists, October 3, 2024. CPJ reported four more journalists were charged under the Cybercrimes Act despite the February reform. That undercuts any claim that 2024 produced a cleaner information environment. QIDs: `4B.10`, `4B.6`, `4B.9`, `4B.5`.

- [Nigeria: Government warnings raise concerns about upcoming protests](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/07/29/nigerian-government-warnings-raise-concerns-about-upcoming-protests) — Human Rights Watch, July 29, 2024. HRW said officials were already framing the planned protests as regime-change activity and warning of chaos and violence. This is negative evidence for tolerating opposition mobilization as normal democratic contestation. QIDs: `4B.10`, `4B.1`, `4B.3`, `4B.7`.

- [Nigeria charges 76, including minors, with treason after August protests](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/nigeria-charges-76-including-minors-with-treason-after-august-protests-3698000) — Reuters via Investing.com, November 1, 2024. Reuters reported treason charges against 76 defendants, including minors, after the August protests. That is strong evidence of punitive escalation rather than democratic resilience. QIDs: `4B.10`, `4B.1`, `4B.3`, `4B.4`, `4B.7`, `4B.8`.

- [Nigeria police used excessive force to violently quash #EndBadGovernance protests](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/11/nigeria-police-used-excessive-force-to-violently-quash-endbadgovernance-protests/) — Amnesty International, November 28, 2024. Amnesty documented killings, mass detentions, torture claims, and denial of wrongdoing during the crackdown. That is the clearest evidence that 2024 left protest space and accountability weaker, not stronger. QIDs: `4B.10`, `4B.3`, `4B.4`, `4B.7`.

- [Nigeria considers tough penalties for subversive acts under proposed law](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/nigeria-considers-tough-penalties-for-subversive-acts-under-proposed-law-3571782) — Reuters via Investing.com, August 14, 2024. Reuters reported a proposed Counter Subversion Bill that critics said was aimed at cracking down on dissent after the protests. Even though it was later withdrawn, the proposal itself is negative evidence for democratic resilience. QIDs: `4B.10`, `4B.1`, `4B.3`, `4B.6`, `4B.7`.

**Overall read**

Tinubu’s 2024 record is not one of formal constitutional rupture, but it is also not one of democratic strengthening. The positive side is mostly rhetorical or procedural: dialogue, constitutional review, ordinary cabinet reshuffling, and no internet shutdown. The negative side is more concrete: repression of protests, criminalization of dissent, harassment of journalists, and digital-law pressure. Net effect: **political freedom and democratic resilience appear weaker than what he inherited in 2024**.

**Search gap**

I did not find direct 2024 evidence of Tinubu trying to extend his term, cancel elections, or block a constitutional transfer of power. The judgment here rests on the year’s treatment of opposition, protest, media, and digital freedom rather than on a formal succession crisis.
